title: Crystal Palace Emergency Help Points
summary: Emergency health facilities, runoff hazards, and essential supply points for Crystal Palace.
content: For life-threatening emergencies, call 999 immediately. 1. Nearest Hospitals with 24-Hour A&E: - Croydon University Hospital (530 London Road, Thornton Heath, CR7 7YE). Directions from Crystal Palace Station: ~45 min walk south-west via Anerley Road and Whitehorse Road (2.4 miles), or take bus 468 south to London Road. - King's College Hospital (Denmark Hill, London SE5 9RS) — Designated Major Trauma Centre. Directions from Crystal Palace Station: take Southern/Overground rail direct to Denmark Hill, or bus 3 north through Dulwich (~3.8 miles). 2. NHS Urgent Treatment Centres: - Croydon Urgent Treatment Centre (Croydon University Hospital, 530 London Road, CR7 7YE). Walk-in facility for non-life-threatening cuts, burns, sprains, and acute conditions. Open 24 hours. - Beckenham Beacon Urgent Treatment Centre (379 Croydon Road, Beckenham, BR3 3QL). Directions from Anerley Station: ~30 min walk east along Croydon Road (1.5 miles), or take bus 356 east. 3. Local Hazard Notes: Crystal Palace sits on a prominent ridge (112m elevation). Hazards include severe surface water runoff down steep gradients (Anerley Hill, Gipsy Hill, South Norwood Hill) during torrential storms, with flooding pooling rapidly in valley basins below. 4. Essential Supplies: Pharmacies and grocery stores in the Crystal Palace Triangle (Westow Hill, Westow Street, and Church Road) stock medical supplies, batteries, and potable water. Note: addresses and opening hours may have changed — confirm on arrival where possible.
